To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most negative potential reached during cyclic voltammetry is −0.54 V, which does not exceed the safe limit for water electrolysis; that the most positive potential reached is 0.59 V, also below the safe limit for electrolysis; and that the maximum polarization during excitation is below 0.5 V.
the most negative potential across the electrode–liquid interface reached −0 .54 V, which did not exceed the potential limits for water reduction.
the multi-electrody spiral nerve cuff electrode, which is a promising device to be used for peripheral nerve stimulation, can safely operate within the potential window of water electrolysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a multi-electrodes spiral cuff to be applied in selective nerve stimulation.
the development of a multi-electroded cuff to be implanted on the vagal nerve for the treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
the development of a multi-electrodes spiral cuff to be implanted around the left cervical vagus of the porcine animal model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the investigated multi-electrode cuff with a platinum electrode is suitable for selective stimulation of the vagus nerve.
the tested stimulation pulse is suitable for efficient and reversible stimulation, while the electrode is suitable for efficient, safe and reversible selective nerve stimulation.
the investigated platinum electrode within a half-cuff can be safely used for selective nerve stimulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a safe and efficient electrode is developed and the electrochemical performance has been investigated.

the electrode can be used in selective nerve stimulations with quasitrapazoidal biphasic currents, with a pulse amplitude of 2.5–4.0 mA, pulse duration of 0.5–1.0 ms and interphase interval of 1–1.5 ms.

the electrochemical properties of the platinum electrodes within the half-cuff, tested by selective stimulation of the isolated nerve, were found to be sufficient for safe and efficient stimulation of nerves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to use the half-cuff for selective nerve stimulation, as the charge injection capacity is high enough to stimulate the nerve.
the charge injection capacity of a platinum electrode is significantly larger than its cathodal charge storage, which is a result of the electrode being able to reversibly store charge.
the electrochemical performance is strongly dependent on the electrode geometry.
